subject: airliner cockpit
title: What If a Cockpit Window Blew Out Mid-Flight? In 1990 the Captain Went With It

scenes.text: What if the cockpit window blew out at 17,000 feet? In 1990 the captain went with it.
June 10, 1990. British Airways flight 5390, Birmingham to Malaga, 81 passengers. Thirteen minutes in, a bang.
The windscreen is gone. Captain Tim Lancaster is blasted out of his seat, legs caught on the controls, body pinned outside.
Flight attendant Nigel Ogden grabs his belt. When his arms give out, two more crew take over.
The co-pilot flies alone. Twenty minutes later he lands at Southampton. Lancaster is alive: frostbite, a broken arm, wrist and thumb.
The cause: a windscreen fitted 27 hours earlier with 84 bolts fractionally too thin. Lancaster was flying again within five months.

description:
What if the cockpit windscreen blew out in flight? On 10 June 1990, British Airways Flight 5390 lost its left windscreen 13 minutes after takeoff at about 17,300 feet; Captain Tim Lancaster was blown halfway out of the aircraft and held by the legs by cabin crew for 20 minutes while co-pilot Alastair Aitchison landed at Southampton.
Lancaster survived with frostbite and fractures to his arm, wrist and thumb and returned to flying in under five months. The windscreen had been fitted 27 hours earlier with 84 bolts fractionally too small in diameter.
